memoryText: To him all the prophets bear witness that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Acts 10:43 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Peter says this in the house of Cornelius, a Roman, in the first sermon to the Gentiles. In one verse, he sums up the gospel.

“To him all the prophets bear witness.” The Old Testament is a witness to Jesus. Moses, David, Isaiah, and the others all point to him. This is why we read the whole Bible as one story.

“That everyone who believes in him.” Notice the word “everyone.” The offer is universal, to Jew and Gentile, to the devout and the sinner. The one condition is belief: trust in Jesus.

“Receives forgiveness of sins.” Forgiveness is the great need and the great gift. It is received, not earned. The word “receives” means we hold out empty hands.

“Through his name.” Forgiveness comes through his name, that is, through who he is and what he has done. We do not come in our own name or by our own merit.

When you wonder whether the gospel is really for you, or whether you are too far from God, say this verse. It was spoken to a Gentile soldier, and it is for everyone who believes.
weekInReview: This week the gospel moved out from Jerusalem. After Stephen’s death, the church was scattered, and Philip took the word to Samaria and met an Ethiopian official reading Isaiah 53. You saw the risen Jesus stop Saul on the road to Damascus and ask, “Why are you persecuting me?” You watched God show Peter in a vision that he should not call any person common or unclean, and then pour out the Holy Spirit on Cornelius’s Gentile household. The Antioch church, full of Jews and Greeks, set apart Barnabas and Saul, and Paul preached to the Gentiles in Pisidian Antioch, citing Isaiah 49:6. Psalm 67 and Psalm 87 gave you songs for the nations: the blessing that spills over to the world and the city where former enemies are registered as born in Zion.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus asked Saul, “Why are you persecuting me?” What does it mean that Christ identifies so closely with his people?
God told Peter, “What God has made clean, do not call common.” Who do you tend to see as outside the reach of the gospel, and how could God change that?
Psalm 67 prays for God’s blessing so that all nations will praise him. How does that change how you think about your own blessings?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that everyone who believes in Jesus receives forgiveness.
Thank him for sending his word to the nations.
